title: JANUS Tear Guided-Policy Candidate

source_bridge.computational_translation: A compact independently checkable invariant condensed from one or more residual SAT states.
source_bridge.metaphor_boundary: The metaphor supplies a name only. Every complexity claim requires an explicit extractor, verifier, state policy, and worst-case bound.

positive_result.tear: one component-charge parity bit per connected component
positive_result.result: A family-specific global invariant distinguishes formulas whose bounded-local signatures coincide.

falsified_candidates.name: bounded-local complete tear language
falsified_candidates.reason: C017 local SAT/UNSAT twins and later high-treewidth descendants have equal bounded-radius signed-incidence views with opposite labels.

falsified_candidates.name: unsigned structure plus signed marginal complete tear
falsified_candidates.reason: An exact three-variable SAT/UNSAT pair shares unsigned scopes, clause and variable sign marginals, primal graph, component sizes, and recognized XOR inventory.

falsified_candidates.name: polynomial continuation-complete quotient of all residual states
falsified_candidates.reason: For E_n(X,Y)=AND_i(x_i<->y_i), assigning X produces 2^n residuals that are pairwise distinguishable by Y continuations although E_n has O(n) size.

tear_trilemma.decision_only: At most two classes exist, but computing the class is SAT itself and is circular.
tear_trilemma.continuation_complete: The equality family forces exponentially many classes, so the strong all-state form is false.
tear_trilemma.policy_selected: A polynomial-time policy that visits polynomially many states and always decides SAT is already a polynomial-time SAT algorithm.

surviving_candidate.statement: There exists one explicitly defined polynomial-time tear language and transition policy that generates only polynomially many polynomially verifiable tears and states on every CNF, returns a witness on SAT inputs, and returns a sound polynomially checkable rejection artifact otherwise.
surviving_candidate.conditional_consequence: Such a construction would put SAT in P and therefore prove P=NP.

next_falsification_gates: fix a finite candidate tear language
attack equivalent encodings and hidden parity
claim_boundary: The strong universal quotient was refuted. The surviving policy-selected form is essentially an explicit P=NP algorithmic target, not a solution obtained from failure to find a counterexample.
